meta.title: Prompt optimizer
meta.description: Rewrite a prompt into a structured specification — a lead sentence plus 4–7 numbered requirement groups with concrete sub-items — filling in the implementation conventions this class of task normally needs, while variables, fenced and inline code, URLs, quoted text, and numbers stay byte-identical. Click the icon-only sparkle button in the composer's tool row to rewrite the draft in place; when it finishes, **Send** appears so the optimized prompt can go out immediately, and **Undo** restores the previous draft. You can also trigger it yourself with `/optimize [--mode user|system|message] [--goal clarity|structure|concise|professional|creative|technical] [--template generic|professional|analytical|concise|output-format|conversation] [--format structured|plain] <prompt>`. The agent can also call the `optimize_prompt` tool when you ask it to improve a prompt; its result appears as a card showing the optimized text, the original for comparison, a change summary, warnings, and a copy button. Each run makes exactly one model call, through the model already configured in DSH or, when `modelSource` is `byok`, through your own OpenAI-compatible endpoint; the prompt text goes to that endpoint and nowhere else. The plugin never rewrites or sends a message on its own initiative — sending only ever follows your click on **Send**. It never invents facts, data, links, or citations, and the parameters it picked are listed as assumptions. When verification shows that protected content was destroyed, it returns the original text unchanged and says why. The original and the result are recorded in the session log as ordinary tool output, and cached in memory for ten minutes by default. Set `composerButton: false` to remove the button and `format: plain` for prose output. Turning the plugin off removes the button, the tool, the command, and the card; it leaves no background work.
